NEW YORK, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NYSE American: ATNM) ("Actinium" or the "Company"), a pioneer in the development of targeted radiotherapies, today announced an inducement equity award to a newly hired non-executive employee.

On October 26, 2026, the Company granted the employee a non-qualified stock option to purchase 3,000 shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $1.40 per share, equal to the closing price of Actinium's common stock on the NYSE American on October 26, 2026. The option has a ten-year term; 28% of the shares underlying the option vest on the first anniversary of the grant date, and the remainder vest in equal monthly installments of 2% of the shares underlying the option over the following 36 months.

Vesting of the award is subject to the employee's continued service with the Company through the applicable vesting date. The award was granted outside of the Company's Amended and Restated 2019 Stock Plan as an inducement material to the employee's entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Section 711(a) of the NYSE American Company Guide, and is subject to the terms of the Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 2026 Employment Inducement Award Plan and the applicable award agreement.

About Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

Actinium is a pioneer in targeted radiotherapies designed to improve outcomes for patients with cancer. The company employs a biology-driven approach to develop differentiated radiopharmaceuticals for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. Its mission is to transform cancer treatment through innovative radioconjugates that maximize therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity to healthy tissue by combining expertise in tumor biology, translational medicine, and radiochemistry. Since inception, Actinium has focused on developing innovative radiotherapies. Its pipeline reflects this strategy across three areas: (1) solid tumor therapeutics including ATNM-400 and Actimab-A with pan-tumor potential; (2) Actimab-A as a therapeutic backbone for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) in collaboration with the National Cancer Institute (NCI); and (3) targeted conditioning agents including Iomab-B for bone marrow transplant and Iomab-ACT for cell and gene therapy conditioning. ATNM-400 targets a novel antigen distinct from PSMA and has demonstrated preclinical activity across metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and breast cancer, and is being evaluated in a first-in-human Phase 1 study in mCRPC. Actimab-A has shown improved survival in relapsed/refractory AML with CLAG-M and is advancing toward a Phase 2/3 trial, with additional development ongoing through a CRADA with the NCI. Actinium is also advancing preclinical solid tumor programs and holds ~250 patents and patent applications, including intellectual property related to cyclotron-based production of Ac-225. For more information, please visit www.actiniumpharma.com.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. (the "Company" or "Prospect Ridge") (CSE:PRR)(OTCQB:PRRSF)(FRA:0ED) is pleased to announce that it has closed the third and final tranche of its non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") of $0.075 critical mineral flow-through units (the "FT Units") first announced on October 2, 2026, and updated on October 13th, 19th and 21st, 2026 (see news releases for details), issuing an aggregate of 2,016,669 FT Units for gross proceeds of $151,250.18. All securities issued in the third tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring on March 1, 2027.

Each FT Unit was comprised of one flow-through common share (a "Common Share") in the capital of the Company and one-half of one Common Share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one common share at a price of $0.10 for a period of two years after closing, subject to accelerated expiry if the Company's common shares trade or close on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "Exchange") at $0.21or more for ten consecutive trading days.

In connection with the third tranche, the Company paid aggregate finder fees of $8,487.51 in cash and issued an aggregate of 113,167 finder warrants having the same terms as the warrants comprised in the FT Units (exercisable at $0.10 for two years subject to acceleration on the occurrence of certain events). There was no insider participation in the third tranche.

Over the three tranches, the Company raised aggregate gross proceeds of $1,836,375 through the issue of 24,485,004 FT Units, representing an oversubscription of $336,375 over the originally planned Offering of $1,500,000.

Over the three tranches, insiders purchased an aggregate of 335,000 FT Units, which as of the third tranche closing represented less than 1% of the then issued and outstanding shares, and less than 1% if the associated warrants were immediately exercised. The participation by insiders constitutes a "related party transaction" within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company has relied upon the exemption from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements pursuant to sections 5.5(a), (b) and (c), and sections 5.7(1)(a) and (b), respectively, of MI 61-101.

Use of Proceeds of the Offering

The Company intends to use the gross proceeds from the FT Shares to incur, on its mineral projects in British Columbia, eligible "Canadian exploration expenses" that will also qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" under the Income Tax Act. The Company intends the bulk of the gross proceeds to finance an upcoming 2,500-meter drill program on the Issuer's Camelot project, located near Horsefly, B.C. (see News Releases dated January 23, February 25 and June 16, 2026) and for preparations for an extensive Spring drill program at the Company's Excalibur project located north of Smithers, B.C (see News Releases dated September 10 and 24, 2026).

The securities to be offered under the Offering have not been, and will not be, registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act") or any U.S. state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, United States persons absent registration or any applicable exemption from the registration requirements of the U.S. Securities Act and applicable U.S. state securities laws. This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy securities in the United States, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. is a British Columbia-based exploration and development company focused on critical metals and gold. VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Revolve Renewable Power Corp. (CSE:REVV)(OTCQB:REVVF) ("Revolve" or the "Company"), a North American owner, operator and developer of power generation and digital infrastructure projects, is pleased to announce that, through a subsidiary, it has entered into a definitive agreement for the acquisition (the "Acquisition") of all of the issued and outstanding shares in the capital of Logan Energy Storage ULC ("Logan"). Logan owns a portfolio of three battery energy storage system ("BESS") projects located in Ontario (the "Portfolio"), with a total capacity of 6 megawatts ("MW") / 11.7 MWh. The total purchase price for the Portfolio is CAD$1,500,000 and will be funded by cash on the Company's balance sheet. The seller of the Logan is arm's length to Revolve.

The Company executed definitive equity purchase and related agreements October 30, 2026, providing for the Acquisition, which remains subject to customary closing conditions and applicable approvals. Upon closing, the Acquisition is expected to increase Revolve's battery storage capacity in Ontario to approximately 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh across nine projects. It builds on the Company's acquisition of the six-project, 14.2 MW / 24.3 MWh Trillium Storage portfolio, completed in August 2026.

"The Logan acquisition is another important step for Revolve as we continue to build our storage platform in Ontario," said Myke Clark, CEO. "Following the completion of Trillium, this transaction is expected to increase our battery storage capacity in the province and further establish our presence in Ontario. We look forward to closing the transaction and building on this platform as we continue to execute our disciplined acquisition and development strategy."

The transaction reflects Revolve's continued strategy of acquiring assets alongside its greenfield development pipeline.

Revolve was formed in 2012 to capitalize on the growing global demand for renewable power. Revolve develops utility-scale wind, solar, hydro and battery storage projects in the US, Canada and Mexico. RICHMOND, Ind., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., a Maryland corporation (the "Company") (NASDAQ: RMBI), parent company of First Bank Midwest, today reported net income of $1.7 million, or diluted earnings per share of $0.11, for the third quarter of 2026. This compares to net income of $2.2 million, or $0.22 diluted earnings per share, for the second quarter of 2026, and net income of $3.6 million, or diluted earnings per share of $0.36, for the third quarter of 2025.

The decrease in net income from the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to higher provision for credit losses, as well as noninterest expense. The provision for credit losses totaled $6.1 million during the third quarter of 2026, compared to $823,000 in the prior quarter and $269,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in provision was primarily due to the need to replenish and increase the allowance for credit losses following $6.1 million of net charge-offs during the quarter, including a partial charge-off of $4.5 million on a nonaccruing commercial real estate loan, which was transferred to other real estate owned during the current quarter, and an $803,000 charge-off on a commercial and industrial loan, as well as an increase in non-performing loans. In addition, noninterest expense during the quarter included $3.0 million of nonrecurring merger-related expenses associated with the acquisition of Farmers Bancorp. These items were partially offset by a preliminary bargain purchase gain recognized on the Company's acquisition of Farmers Bancorp of $1.6 million.

Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.8 million, or $0.56 diluted earnings per share, compared to net income of $8.2 million, or $0.82 diluted earnings per share, for the same period in 2025.

On July 1, 2026, the Company completed its previously announced merger with Farmers Bancorp pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated November 11, 2025. Immediately thereafter, The Farmers Bank merged with and into First Bank Richmond. The combined company continues to operate as Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., while the combined bank is operating under the name First Bank Midwest. The combined company continues to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker symbol "RMBI." The administrative headquarters of the holding company remains in Richmond, Indiana, while the combined bank is headquartered in Frankfort, Indiana.

The financial results presented in this earnings release reflect the Company's operations following the completion of the merger on July 1, 2026.  Accordingly, the Company's financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, include the operating results of the combined company. Financial results for periods prior to July 1, 2026, reflect the operations of Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., on a standalone basis, and do not include the operations of Farmers Bancorp.

Message from the Chairman and CEO

Garry Kleer, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, commented, "Our third quarter results reflected the impact of our merger with Farmers Bancorp, which significantly expanded our balance sheet and increased net interest income compared to both the prior quarter and the third quarter of last year. Earnings were impacted by a higher provision for credit losses and increased noninterest expense. As we move forward, our focus remains on successfully integrating the two organizations, realizing the strategic benefits of the combination and continuing to serve our customers and communities."

Third Quarter Performance Highlights

  • Net interest income increased by $10.8 million, or 89.2%, to $22.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $12.1 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Net interest income increased by $11.6 million, or 102.3%, from $11.3 million for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • Annualized net interest margin was 3.68% for the current quarter, compared to 3.22% in the prior quarter and 3.07% for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • A provision for credit losses of $6.1 million was recorded for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $823,000 and $269,000 for the quarters ended June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.
  • Noninterest income increased $3.0 million to $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and increased $3.3 million from $1.3 million for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • Noninterest expense increased $9.8 million to $20.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which included $3.0 million in nonrecurring merger-related expenses, compared to $10.2 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and increased $11.9 million from $8.1 million for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • Assets totaled $2.60 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.55 billion at June 30, 2026 and $1.53 billion at December 31, 2025.
  • Loans and leases, net of allowance for credit losses, totaled $2.00 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.21 billion at June 30, 2026,  and $1.18 billion at December 31, 2025.
  • Non-performing loans and leases totaled $32.2 million, or 1.59% of total loans and leases, at September 30, 2026, compared to $21.8 million, or 1.78%, at June 30, 2026, and $17.4 million, or 1.46%, at December 31, 2025.
  • The allowance for credit losses totaled $25.4 million, or 1.25% of total loans and leases outstanding, at September 30, 2026, compared to $17.0 million, or 1.39%, at June 30, 2026, and $16.5 million, or 1.38%, at December 31, 2025.
  • Deposits totaled $2.09 billion at September 30, 2026 compared to $1.15 billion at June 30, 2026, and $1.11 billion at December 31, 2025. At September 30, 2026, noninterest-bearing deposits totaled $351.4 million, or 16.9% of total deposits, compared to $100.1 million, or 8.7% of total deposits at June 30, 2026, and $100.1 million, or 9.0% of total deposits at December 31, 2025.
  • Stockholders' equity totaled $228.9 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $148.3 million at June 30, 2026, and $145.8 million at December 31, 2025. The Company's equity to assets ratio was 8.81% at September 30, 2026.
  • Book value per share was $13.66 at September 30, 2026, compared to  $14.11 at June 30, 2026 and $13.88 per share at December 31, 2025.
  • The Bank's Tier 1 leverage ratio was 9.99% at September 30, 2026, well in excess of the 8.0% CBLR requirement.

Under the CBLR framework, qualifying institutions that maintain a leverage ratio of greater than 8.0% are deemed to satisfy applicable regulatory capital requirements and are no longer required to calculate risk-based capital ratios for regulatory reporting purposes.

Income Statement Summary

Net Interest Income. Net interest income before the provision for credit losses increased $11.6 million to $22.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $11.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, which significantly expanded the Company's interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. The acquisition also impacted net interest income through the accretion and amortization of fair value adjustments recorded in connection with the transaction.

Annualized net interest margin was 3.68% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.07% for the third quarter of 2025. The increase primarily reflected higher yields and average balances of interest-earning assets resulting from the loan portfolio acquired in the merger, as well as lower average funding costs and a higher volume of noninterest-bearing demand deposits.

Interest Income. Interest income increased $16.7 million to $38.6 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $21.8 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to a $1.02 billion increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets, mainly as a result of the merger with Farmers Bancorp. The average yield on interest-earning assets was 6.20%, compared to 5.93% in the third quarter of 2025.

Interest income on loans and leases increased $14.6 million to $34.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $19.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. This increase was primarily due to an $831.9 million increase in the average balance of loans and leases, mainly reflecting loans acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp. The average yield earned on loans and leases was 6.79% as compared to 6.63% in the same quarter a year ago.

Interest income on investment securities, excluding FHLB stock, increased $1.3 million to $2.9 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, due to a $110.5 million increase in the average balance of securities and a 66 basis point increase in the average yield to 3.25%. The increases were primarily due to securities acquired in the acquisition and the subsequent repositioning of the securities portfolio. Dividends on FHLB stock increased $203,000 to $517,000 during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $7.1 million increase in the average balance of FHLB stock held.

Interest income on cash and cash equivalents increased $623,000 to $826,000 during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase from the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to increased cash balances maintained following the merger with Farmers Bancorp.

Interest Expense. Interest expense increased $5.2 million to $15.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase was due to a $728.8 million increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities, primarily as a result of the merger with Farmers Bancorp, partially offset by a decrease in the average rate paid. The average rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities during the third quarter of 2026 was 3.17%, compared to 3.35% in the third quarter of 2025.

Interest expense on deposits increased $4.9 million to $12.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to a $710.5 million increase in the average balance of interest-bearing deposits as a result of the merger with Farmers Bancorp, partially offset by a decrease in the average rate paid. The average rate paid on interest-bearing deposits was 2.98% and 3.14% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.  Within interest-bearing deposits, the average rate paid on interest-bearing checking accounts increased to 2.19% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.17% for the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to public fund accounts acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, which pay higher rates to municipal depositors.

Interest expense on borrowings increased $266,000 to $3.0 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. The average balance of borrowings totaled $284.1 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $265.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the average balance was primarily due to subordinated debt assumed in the merger with Farmers Bancorp. The average rate paid on borrowings was 4.26% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 4.16% for the third quarter of 2025.

Provision for Credit Losses. A provision for credit losses of $6.1 million was recorded in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $269,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the need to replenish the allowance following a $4.5 million partial charge-off recorded upon the transfer of a commercial real estate property to other real estate owned and an $803,000 charge-off on a commercial and industrial loan, as well as an increase in non-performing loans during the quarter. The related commercial real estate loan was placed on nonaccrual status in the second quarter of 2026, and the Company took possession of the property late in the third quarter. Net charge-offs for the third quarter of 2026 were $6.1 million, compared to $317,000 in the third quarter of 2025. No provision for credit losses was recorded at acquisition on loans acquired in the merger, as the initial allowance on those loans was established through the gross-up approach described under "Allowance for Credit Losses."

Noninterest Income. Total noninterest income increased $3.3 million to $4.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase included a $1.6 million preliminary bargain purchase gain in connection with the merger with Farmers Bancorp. Excluding this gain, noninterest income increased $1.6 million, primarily reflecting the larger customer base following the merger, including increases of $415,000 in service charges on deposit accounts and $1.1 million in other income primarily related to wealth management income.

Noninterest Expense. Total noninterest expense increased $11.9 million to $20.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, which significantly expanded the Company's operating infrastructure and employee base. The quarter also included $3.0 million in nonrecurring merger-related expenses, consisting primarily of software and core conversion expenses. In addition, noninterest expense was impacted by $1.8 million in amortization expense related to the core deposit intangible recognized in connection with the merger.

Income Tax Expense. Income tax expense decreased $1.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The Company recognized an income tax benefit of $482,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to income tax expense of $645,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $1.1 million decrease was primarily attributable to lower pre-tax income and favorable tax effects from a preliminary bargain purchase gain, higher tax credits and increased tax-exempt interest income, partially offset by nondeductible transaction costs.

Balance Sheet Summary

General. Total assets increased $1.07 billion to $2.60 billion at September 30, 2026, as compared to $1.53 billion at December 31, 2025, primarily due to $1.2 billion in assets acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp.

Investment Securities. Investment securities increased $75.1 million to $329.8 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $254.7 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to $205.0 million in available for sale securities acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp. Offsetting this increase were sales of $91.9 million of securities acquired. The proceeds from sales were used to pay off FHLB advances assumed in the merger.

Loans and Leases. Loans and leases increased $827.2 million to $2.00 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.18 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to $803.6 million in loans acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp, with the remaining $23.6 million reflecting organic loan growth.

Non-performing loans and leases, consisting of nonaccrual loans and leases and accruing loans and leases 90 days or more past due, totaled $32.2 million, or 1.59% of total loans and leases, at September 30, 2026, compared to $17.4 million, or 1.46%, at December 31, 2025. Nonaccrual loans and leases increased $17.4 million to $30.6 million at September 30, 2026, from $13.2 million at December 31, 2025. The increase in non-performing loans and leases was primarily due to $4.8 million of loans and leases that were non-performing when acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, $1.1 million of acquired loans and leases that became non-performing after the acquisition, and $8.9 million of legacy loans and leases that became non-performing during the period, primarily consisting of commercial and industrial loans associated with one customer relationship. 

Allowance for Credit Losses. The allowance for credit losses on loans and leases increased $8.9 million to $25.4 million, or 1.25% of total loans and leases, at September 30, 2026, from $16.5 million, or 1.38% of total loans and leases, at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to the initial allowance for credit losses of $8.3 million established on loans acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, including $699,000 on purchased credit-deteriorated loans and $7.6 million on purchased seasoned loans, and a provision for credit losses of $7.6 million, partially offset by net charge-offs of $7.0 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The Company early adopted ASU 2025-08, Financial Instruments - Credit Losses  (Topic 326): Purchased Loans, and applied the gross-up approach to the purchased seasoned loans. Under this approach, the initial allowance on those loans was recorded as an adjustment to their amortized cost basis at acquisition, rather than through provision expense. As a result, no day-one provision for credit losses was recognized on loans acquired in the merger. The allowance for credit losses provided coverage of 78.9% of non-performing loans and leases at September 30, 2026, compared to 94.6% at December 31, 2025. The decrease in the allowance as a percentage of total loans and leases primarily reflects lower expected credit loss rates on the acquired loan portfolio relative to the legacy portfolio. The decrease in the allowance as a percentage of non-performing loans and leases primarily reflects the $14.8 million increase in non-performing loans and leases, a significant portion of which are collateral-dependent loans requiring limited specific reserves based on the estimated fair value of the underlying collateral. Net charge-offs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $7.0 million, or an annualized 0.64% of average loans and leases, compared to $1.3 million for the comparable period of 2025.

Management regularly evaluates credit exposure across its loan portfolio and within its geographic markets. As of September 30, 2026, the Company's credit risk assessment incorporated ongoing economic conditions, including inflationary pressures, capital market volatility, and geopolitical risks. Management continues to conduct portfolio stress testing and monitor credit metrics and believes the allowance for credit losses is appropriate based on the current composition of the loan and lease portfolio and the level of individually evaluated reserves.

Other Assets. Other assets increased $66.6 million to $97.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $31.0 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, including the recognition of a core deposit intangible asset of $22.9 million, a $20 million increase in the cash surrender value of bank-owned life insurance, a $4.8 million increase in accrued interest receivable and a $1.4 million increase in mortgage servicing rights. At September 30, 2026, the carrying value of the core deposit intangible was $21.2 million.

Included in other assets, other real estate owned totaled $2.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $56,000 at December 31, 2025.  The increase was primarily due to the transfer of two commercial real estate properties to other real estate owned during the third quarter of 2026: a former behavioral health hospital campus located in Dayton, Ohio, with a carrying value of $2.2 million, and a restaurant property located in Richmond, Indiana, with a carrying value of $450,000. Both properties were recorded at fair value less estimated costs to sell at the time of transfer.  The Company is actively marketing both properties for sale.

Deposits. Total deposits increased $970.5 million to $2.09 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.11 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase in deposits from December 31, 2025 was primarily due to $935.8 million in deposits acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp. Brokered time deposits totaled $268.1 million, or 12.9% of total deposits, at September 30, 2026, compared to $235.9 million, or 21.2% of total deposits at December 31, 2025. Noninterest-bearing demand deposits totaled $351.4 million at September 30, 2026 compared to $100.1 million at December 31, 2025, and were 16.9% and 9.0% of total deposits at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively.

Borrowings. Total borrowings increased $11.6 million to $263.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $252.0 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to the $14.5 million in subordinated debt assumed in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, partially offset by the repayment of other FHLB advances. The Company also assumed approximately $95 million in FHLB advances in the merger, all of which were repaid during the quarter with proceeds from the sale of available for sale securities acquired in the merger.

Stockholders' Equity. Stockholders' equity totaled $228.9 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $83.1 million from December 31, 2025. The increase in stockholders' equity was primarily attributable to the issuance of 6,254,286 shares of common stock due to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, resulting in an increase to equity of $99.3 million, and net income of $6.8 million. Offsetting these increases were an increase to other comprehensive loss of $18.5 million, reflecting an increase in net unrealized losses on available-for-sale securities, net of tax, due to higher market interest rates during the period, and $5.3 million in dividends paid to Company stockholders.

SUN VALLEY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Mission Valley Bancorp (OTCQX: MVLY, “Mission Valley”, or the “Company”) announced today net income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $2.1 million, or $0.62 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $3.8 million, or $1.11 per diluted share, compared to net income of $4.9 million, or $1.45 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Tamara Gurney, Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bancorp, commented, “We are pleased with the year-to-date growth of $15.2 million, or 10.1% annualized, in our non-interest bearing core deposits, particularly during a very challenging time to attract and retain core deposits for the industry as a whole. This supported gross loan growth of $6.4 million, after selling $13.4 million in SBA loan principal, for the current quarter. However, the most significant highlight of the quarter was the leadership transition at Mission Valley Bank with Brian Carlson being appointed President and Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bank as I stepped in to the role of Executive Chair and CEO of Mission Valley Bancorp. Brian will be instrumental in shaping the path forward for the Company and the Bank.”

Brian Carlson, President and Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bank and President of Mission Valley Bancorp, commented, “We were able to produce solid net income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the quarter despite the impact from the industry-wide headwinds on SBA lending volume and the increase in our provision for credit losses primarily due to one charged-off commercial loan. The quality of our SBA loan portfolio remains strong with low levels of past due, non-accrual, classified loans, and overall default rates that continue to outperform industry averages. In addition, secondary market premiums on SBA loans remain at favorable levels as we continue to grow the SBA loan portfolio, while maintaining our asset quality.”

Mr. Carlson continued, “As we look ahead to the fourth quarter and closing out 2026, we look forward to the full launch of one of our digital transformation initiatives and we will be focused on executing certain strategic and proactive measures with respect to our loan and investment portfolios to reposition and strengthen our balance sheet for 2027 and beyond.”

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Net Income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Net Interest Income was $8.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $0.5 million, or 7.01%, compared to the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net Interest Margin was 4.47% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 4.54% for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-Interest Income was $2.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $0.5 million, or 17.98%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. Non-Interest Income includes gain on sale of loans and the change in the fair value of Small Business Administration (“SBA”) servicing assets.
  • $13.4 million in loan principal sold resulting in gain on sale of $0.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $17.9 million in loan principal sold and gain on sale of $0.9 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Change in the fair value of SBA servicing assets resulted in a net loss of $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net gain of $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025.

  • Total Deposits were $648.4 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $12.9 million, or 2.03%, compared to December 31, 2025. The $12.9 million growth in Total Deposits was driven by the $15.2 million increase in non-interest bearing deposits, partially offset by the $2.3 million decrease in interest bearing deposits.

  • $397 thousand in net charge-offs on loans in the third quarter of 2026 primarily from one commercial loan, compared to $60 thousand in net recoveries from previously charged-off loans in the third quarter of 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, Classified Loans were comprised of $15.4 million from accounts receivable loans, $8.4 million from commercial loans loans, $7.5 million from real estate loans, and $1.8 million from SBA loans.

  • Provision for Credit Losses was $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The provision in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by the charge-off of one commercial loan.

Grand Falls-Windsor, Newfoundland and Labrador--(Newsfile Corp. - October 30, 2026) - First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) ("First Atlantic" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has entered into an asset purchase agreement dated October 30, 2026 (the "Agreement") with two arm's length parties (together, the "Vendors") to acquire a 100% interest in three mineral licences comprising 209 mineral claims spanning approximately 52.25 square kilometers located in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador (the "Property" or the "North Arm Ophiolite Property") (the "Transaction").

The North Arm Ophiolite Property, in the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex ("BOIC") of western Newfoundland, is prospective for geologic hydrogen, awaruite nickel alloy (Ni₃Fe), copper, platinum group elements (PGEs) and chromium. The Property covers mantle-derived dunite and peridotite rocks, the same type of iron- and magnesium-rich ultramafic rocks that host First Atlantic's awaruite discoveries at the Pipestone XL Project. They also enable serpentinization, the water-rock reaction that produces natural (white) hydrogen. Elsewhere in the BOIC, at the Tablelands, active hydrogen-bearing alkaline springs show that the process is happening today. The same rocks are also targets for stimulated (orange) hydrogen and mineral carbon storage (CO2 Capture). Awaruite forms under the strongly reducing, hydrogen-rich conditions that serpentinization creates, making it both a nickel-cobalt target and an indicator of hydrogen generation. The mantle section also hosts podiform chromite, the same deposit style as the historic high-grade chromite occurrences at Blow Me Down and Springers Hill. Numerous historic high-grade chromite occurrences have been found throughout the various ophiolite packages of the BOIC, yet little metallurgical or mineralogical work has been done to examine potential recovery and processing methods. The North Arm Ophiolite Property has seen limited modern exploration and has not been systematically tested for hydrogen or awaruite (a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy).

The Property consists of three mineral licences totalling 209 claim cells (5,225 hectares), on the north shore of North Arm, Bay of Islands. Boats can land directly on the Property, and the nearest road comes within 5 km of it. The claims cover the North Arm Mountain massif, one of the four massifs of the Lower Ordovician BOIC. The BOIC is one of the best-preserved sections of oceanic crust and upper mantle in the world. The North Arm Ophiolite Property lies 25 km north of the Company's Ophiolite-X Project, which covers the Blow Me Down and Lewis Hills ophiolites, and extends FAN's control of ultramafic ophiolite complexes in Atlantic Canada to a third BOIC massif.

Terms of the Transaction

Under the Agreement, the Company will acquire the Property in exchange for the issuance of 1,000,000 common shares of the Company (the "Payment Shares") to the Vendors, at a deemed price of $0.55 per share.

PERTH, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Highlights

Second Porphyry Discovery Confirmed at La Verde

  • Assay results for step-out drilling, completed after the reporting period, confirmed the discovery of a second porphyry center – La Verde South - near-doubling the growth potential of the La Verde Project.
  • First step-out Reverse Circulation (RC) drill hole DKP084, located approximately 250 m to the south of La Verde's +0.4% Cu mineralisation footprint, has delivered:
    • 148 m grading 0.44% CuEq1 (0.39% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au) from 36 m
      • Including 44 m grading 0.56% CuEq (0.50% Cu, 0.06 g/t Au) from 138 m
  • First step-out diamond drill hole (DD) DKD100, located a further 100 m to the south of DKP084, also visually recorded a 307 m down-hole interval of copper porphyry-style mineralisation2.
  • Phase 2 resource infill and extensional drilling for La Verde is now complete, following 13 months and over 40,000m of DD and RC drilling, adding to the 10,000 m of RC drilling from Phase 1.

Hot Chili Delivers More Copper-Gold at La Verde

  • Strong assay results continued to be delivered during the quarter from the four drill rigs (2 Diamond and 2 Reverse Circulation) located at La Verde.
  • Continuity of higher-grade copper-gold mineralisation from shallow depths was further confirmed from infill drilling and step out diamond drilling continued to expand the discovery footprint.
  • Standout results reported during the quarter included:
    • DKP063 recorded 398 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.35% Cu, 0.12 g/t Au) from surface
      • Including 62 m grading 0.91% CuEq (0.70% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au) from 20 m
      • Which includes 34 m grading 1.00% CuEq (0.80% Cu, 0.27 g/t Au) from 42 m
    • DKD060 recorded 472 m grading 0.41% CuEq (0.34% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au) from 49 m
      • Including 105.8 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.58% Cu, 0.15 g/t Au) from 397 m
      • Including 32.6 m grading 0.90% CuEq (0.75% Cu, 0.19 g/t Au) from 438 m
    • DKP064 recorded 126 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.38% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au) from 54 m
      • Including 26 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.60% Cu, 0.13 g/t Au) from 108 m
    • DKP078 recorded 240 m grading 0.43% CuEq (0.30% Cu, 0.17 g/t Au) from 36 m
      • Including 54 m grading 0.60% CuEq (0.41% Cu, 0.26 g/t Au) from 46 m
      • And including 42 m grading 0.50% CuEq (0.36% Cu, 0.20 g/t Au) from 188 m
  • The maiden La Verde MRE, revised Costa Fuego PFS and preparation of the EIA submission remained on track, with assay results pending for 35 drill holes (24 infill drilling and 11 southern step-out drillholes).

La Verde Drilling Totals 50,000m, with Phase 2 Now Complete

Strong Cash Position of A$29.3 Million following closure of OR Royalty Amendment Agreement during the quarter.

View PDF version

SUMMARY OF OPERATIONAL ACTIVITIES

Second Porphyry Centre Confirmed at La Verde South

Assay results for step-out drilling, returned after the reporting period, confirmed the discovery of a second porphyry centre at La Verde South. Located immediately south of, and along strike from, the initial La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery, extending the potential mineralisation footprint of La Verde to 1,400m.

The first Reverse Circulation (RC) step-out drill hole, DKP084, was collared approximately 250 m south of La Verde's existing +0.4% Cu mineralisation footprint and returned 148 m grading 0.44% CuEq1 (0.39% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au) from 36 m, including 44 m grading 0.56% CuEq (0.50% Cu, 0.06 g/t Au) from 138 m.

The intersection was primarily oxide copper porphyry-style mineralisation, commencing immediately below shallow gravel cover, and was designed to follow up previously reported RC drill hole DKP024, which recorded 114 m grading 0.4% CuEq (0.4% Cu) from 86 m, including 52 m grading 0.5% CuEq (0.5% Cu, 0.1 g/t Au) from 96 m (see announcement dated 19 May 2025).

The first southern Diamond Drill (DD) step-out drill hole, DKD100, was then collared a further 100 m south of DKP084 to test for higher-grade copper porphyry-style sulphide mineralisation beneath the oxide zone.

DKD100 visually recorded a 307 m downhole interval of copper porphyry-style mineralisation2, comprising oxide mineralisation between 40 m and 172 m and porphyry-style sulphide mineralisation between 172 m and 347 m.

Core photo from DKD100 (259 – 261 m downhole) with vein-hosted and disseminated chalcopyrite (2%) and pyrite (4%) mineralisation in strongly veined tonalite host rock2


1 Copper Equivalent (CuEq) reported for the drillhole intersections were calculated using the following formula: CuEq% = ((Cu% × Cu price 1% per tonne × Cu_recovery) + (Mo ppm × Mo price per g/t × Mo_recovery) + (Au ppm × Au price per g/t × Au_recovery) + (Ag ppm × Ag price per g/t × Ag_recovery)) / (Cu price 1% per tonne × Cu_recovery). The Metal Prices applied in the calculation were: Cu=4.50 USD/lb, Au=3,150 USD/oz, Mo=20 USD/lb, and Ag=30 USD/oz. The entirety of the intersection is assumed as fresh.  The recovery and copper equivalent formula for La Verde uses Cortadera as a proxy, which is considered reasonable given both the similar mineralisation style and amenability testwork completed thus far at La Verde – Recoveries of 83% Cu, 56% Au, 83% Mo and 37% Ag. CuEq (%) = Cu(%) + 0.69 x Au(g/t) + 0.00044 x Mo(ppm) + 0.0043 x Ag(g/t). 

2 Visual estimates of mineral abundance should never be considered a proxy or substitute for laboratory analyses where concentrations or grades are the factor of principal economic interest. Visual estimates also potentially provide no information regarding impurities or deleterious physical properties relevant to valuations. Assay results are pending and will be reported in accordance with the JORC Code (2012) and National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. Sampling methodologies are described in the attached JORC Table 1.

Expansion Drilling Continues to Demonstrate Scale and Continuity

In parallel with southern step-out drilling, drilling across the main La Verde discovery continued to refine the geological interpretation of the mineralised system, further delineating the interpreted high-grade core and demonstrating the vertical and lateral continuity of porphyry-hosted copper-gold mineralisation.

A significant result was returned from DKD060 intersected 472 m grading 0.41% CuEq (0.34% Cu, 0.08g/t Au) from 49 m depth, including a significant higher-grade component comprising 105.8 m grading 0.70% CuEq from 397 m, which also included 32.6 m grading 0.90% CuEq from 438 m (Figure 4).

Results from RC drill hole DKP067 also expanded the lateral extent of mineralisation along La Verde's eastern flank. The drillhole, reported as a partial result, returned 112 m grading 0.47% CuEq (0.40% Cu, 0.10 g/t Au) from 42 m, including 26 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.59% Cu, 0.14 g/t Au) from 62 m.

In-fill RC Drilling Confirms Continuity of Near-Surface, Bulk Mineralisation

RC drill holes targeting the up-dip extension of high-grade mineralisation at La Verde has continued to return wide intersections of copper-gold mineralisation from shallow depths. Importantly, results are distributed across the deposit, highlighting the scale and continuity of La Verde's growing high-grade core.

These results are headlined by DKP063 (Figure 4), which recorded 398 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.35% Cu, 0.12 g/t Au) from surface. Within this, a significant higher-grade component includes 62 m grading 0.91% CuEq (0.70% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au) from just 20 m depth, demonstrating the continuity of high-grade mineralisation at shallow depths and reinforcing the potential for a high-grade starter pit, capable of delivering early higher-grade material to the Costa Fuego mine plan.

DKP075 recorded a partial result of 132 m grading 0.57% CuEq (0.45% Cu, 0.16 g/t Au) from 24 m depth which included 42 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.57% Cu, 0.19 g/t Au) from 96 m (Figure 5). Results for the final 177 m were still outstanding and are expected to be reported shortly.

Additionally, DKP064, which was collared at the southern extent of La Verde's high-grade core, returned 126 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.38% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au) from 54 m depth, including 26 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.60% Cu, 0.13 g/t Au) from 108 m, together with a second intersection of 74 m grading 0.35% CuEq (0.29% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au) from 276 m.

La Verde Drilling Totals 50,000m, with Phase 2 Now Complete

Drilling for the 40,000 m Phase 2 DD and RC program is now complete, following 13 months of progress and bringing the total at La Verde to 50,000 m. The Phase 1 RC program (completed from late 2024 to mid-2025) included 10,000 m and outlined a 750 m x 400 m x 400 m footprint, and in conjunction with Phase 2, has now identified a 1,400 m x 780 m x 800 m footprint across two porphyry centres. Resource infill drilling of La Verde is now complete, and drill rigs will start back up and focus on the growth of La Verde South in early 2027.

Project Development Integration

Since 30 June 2026, Hot Chili has further strengthened the dedicated Costa Fuego project development team and its integrated governance framework for the revised Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) programs, progressing multiple engineering, permitting, social, infrastructure and technical studies.

Key activities advanced include mine-plan inputs, hydrogeological and geotechnical investigations, TSF engineering and water-management studies, and evaluation of power-supply and transmission-line relocation options. Project controls are being consolidated through an integrated P6 schedule, clearer critical-path reporting, risk management and disciplined contractor cost and payment controls.

Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) Continue to Progress

During the quarter preparation of the Costa Fuego environmental approvals continued under the separate EIA 1A (Huasco Water) and EIA 1B (Costa Fuego) workstreams. Unusually heavy rainfall during July and August 2026 affected field activities resulted in delays which have been mitigated in part through four weeks of scheduled contingency. The Q2 2027 submission remains on track for both EIAs.

The two-stream permitting strategy has now been embedded in the project delivery framework:

  • EIA 1A: the seawater intake, pumping and distribution system. Work progressed on the Project Description, environmental chapters, PAS 155 and PAS 156 gap-closure actions, the Punta Huasco Sur protection-area consultation, and flora, vegetation, vertebrate fauna and entomofauna compatibility studies. The latest Project Description revision was under review in October.
  • EIA 1B: baseline studies, engineering inputs and environmental documentation progressed in parallel with the revised PFS2. Archaeological fieldwork was completed, hydrogeological field investigations and packer testing advanced, and the TSF, diversion-water and associated infrastructure packages continue to be developed for incorporation into the assessment.

Costa Fuego Revised PFS Advancement

During the quarter Hot Chili continued to advance workstreams at La Verde, designed to incorporate the new discovery into the Costa Fuego PFS as soon as possible. Geotechnical workstreams were completed at La Verde and are being incorporated into Mineral Resource Estimation and engineering design work, in parallel to metallurgical, hydrogeological and tailings testwork programs.

Analysis of multiple potential materials handling options between La Verde and Productora, the Costa Fuego central processing hub, are also underway. The potential development of a large open-pit mining scenario at Cortadera as an alternative to the previously defined open-pit and underground block cave operation for the later years of Costa Fuego's mine plan is also being finalised.

Social Integration and Community Support

Hot Chili continued its community engagement activities, with a round of early community engagement (Participación Ciudadana Temprana, PCT) in Huasco, Freirina and Vallenar. Public information stands shared details about the Huasco Water project and introduced the Produce Futuro Fund. Additional baseline interviews were completed with a further 9 parties, including 7 Indigenous organisations and 2 neighbourhood associations.

Launched in September, the Produce Futuro Fund will provide grants to successful applicants to support economic development in the Huasco Valley. Hot Chili coordinated the launch and held support sessions to help community members apply. The company received more than 300 applications, with 55 grants to be awarded next quarter.

SUMMARY OF CORPORATE ACTIVITIES

Strategic Partnering Process Update

Hot Chili continues to advance its asset-level strategic Partnering Process, aimed at introducing one or more qualified partners with the financial, technical and operational capability to assist in funding and delivery of the projects.

During the quarter management continued to facilitate ongoing due diligence activities, including arranging site visits, while discussions continued in relation to existing non-binding, indicative, incomplete and conditional proposals received for potential transactions involving the projects. 

The Partnering Process may result in a range of transactions for the Projects. Investors are cautioned that there is no certainty the Partnering Process will result in a transaction or binding agreement.

BMO Capital Markets continues to act as financial adviser in connection with the Partnering Process.

The Company will continue to update the market in accordance with its continuous disclosure obligations.

OR Royalty Amendment Agreement

During the quarter, Hot Chili completed the Amended and Restated Investment Agreement with OR Royalties Inc. ("OR"), receiving net proceeds of A$20.4 million, after transaction costs, from the additional US$15 million royalty investment.

The transaction brings total consideration received under the OR royalty arrangement to US$30 million and expands OR's royalty interest to include the La Verde Project.

The additional non-dilutive funding further strengthens the Company's balance sheet and supports the ongoing advancement of La Verde and the broader Costa Fuego copper-gold development.

The agreement also incorporates an updated change of control buy-back provision, preserving strategic flexibility as the Company progresses its Strategic Partnering Process.

For further details, refer to the Company's announcement dated 7 July 2026.

Cash Position

As of 30 September 2026, the Company had cash of A$29.3 million and no debt.

The operating expenditure for quarter ended 30 September 2026 included payments for staff costs of A$1.3 million and administration and corporate costs of A$1.5 million.

The investing expenditure for quarter ended 30 September 2026 included payments for tenements of A$3.4 million relating mostly to the payment of the San Antonio Purchase Option Agreement for US$2 million, and payments for exploration and evaluation of A$10.1 million relating to drilling (four drill rigs in operation) and development study activities across the La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery, value engineering workstreams and EIA submission activities. This was offset by the receipt of A$20.4 million (net of costs) from the OR Royalty Amendment Agreement.

With the Phase 2 resource infill and extensional drilling program at La Verde scheduled for completion by the end of October 2026, the Company anticipates a material reduction in exploration expenditure in subsequent quarters.

Furthermore, Sociedad Minera El Aguila SpA ("El Aguila") has claimed the following mining exploitation concessions, exercising the preferential rights arising from the corresponding exploration concessions: "Juli 19 1/60", "Juli 20 1/60", "Juli 22 1/60", "Juli 25 1/60", "Julieta 5 1/40", "Julieta 6 1/40", "Julieta 11 1/60", "Julieta 12 1/60", "Julieta 16 1/40" and "Julieta 17 1/40". Conceptual Open Pit Shells

Conceptual open pit shells represent Exploration Targets as defined in the 2012 Edition of the 'Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves' (JORC Code). They are based on completed exploration activities reported in the announcement released 19 May 2025 ('Hot Chili Announces Latest Drill Results for La Verde, Doubling Porphyry Discovery Footprint').

The conceptual open pit shells were generated using copper (Cu) prices of US$3.50/lb Cu and US$6.00/lb Cu on a series of nested Cu grade shells. Other input parameters informing the conceptual open-pit shells (pit slope angles, mining cost, processing cost, etc.) were derived from values reported in the March 2025 Costa Fuego Pre-feasibility Study and are considered appropriate for the style of mineralisation encountered at the La Verde Cu-Au porphyry discovery.

Any potential quantity and grade of the Exploration Target shown is conceptual in nature. There has been insufficient exploration to estimate a Mineral Resource within the target area, and it is uncertain if further exploration will result in the estimation of a Mineral Resource.

Further exploration activities are detailed in this announcement and include (but may not necessarily be limited to) a program of diamond drill holes aiming to extend the mineralised footprint at La Verde. Drilling commenced on 22 September 2025, with the length of the program dependent on a number of considerations including (but not limited to) the results of the exploration activities and regulatory applications and approvals.

PISCATAWAY, N.J., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BHAV Acquisition Corp II (the “Company” or “BHAV”) today announced the closing of its previously announced initial public offering of 10,000,000 units (the “Offering”) at an offering price of $10.00 per unit, with each unit consisting of one Class A ordinary share and one right. Each right entitles the holder to receive one-fourth (1/4) of one Class A ordinary share upon consummation of the Company’s initial business combination. The units began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market (“Nasdaq”) under the ticker symbol “BHAIU” on October 29, 2026. Once the securities comprising the units begin separate trading, the Class A ordinary shares and rights are expected to trade on Nasdaq under the symbols “BHAI” and “BHAIR,” respectively.

Concurrently with the closing of the Offering, the Company closed on a private placement of 225,000 private placement units purchased by BHAV Partners II LLC, the Company’s sponsor, at a price of $10.00 per unit, resulting in gross proceeds of $2,250,000. The private placement units are identical to the units sold in the Offering, subject to limited exceptions described in the prospectus relating to the Offering. Of the proceeds received from the consummation of the Offering and concurrent private placement, an amount equal to $100,500,000 (or $10.05 per unit sold in the Offering) was deposited into a trust account with Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company acting as trustee upon the closing of the Offering.

BHAV intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering and the concurrent private placement of units to pursue and consummate a business combination. BHAV is led by Giri Devanur, Chief Executive Officer and Director, and Chaitanya Kumar Setti, Chief Financial Officer and Director.

Maxim Group LLC acted as the sole book-running manager for the Offering.

The Company has granted the underwriter a 45-day option to purchase up to 1,500,000 additional units at the Offering price less the underwriting discount to cover over-allotments, if any.

A registration statement on Form S-1 (File No. 333-299203) (as amended, the “Registration Statement”) relating to the securities to be sold in the Offering was declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on October 28, 2026. The Offering was made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the prospectus relating to this Offering may be obtained from Maxim Group LLC, 300 Park Avenue, 16th Floor, New York, NY 10022, Attention: Syndicate Department, by telephone at (212) 895-3745 or by email at syndicate@maximgrp.com, or by accessing the SEC’s website, www.sec.gov.

This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

BHAV Acquisition Corp II is a blank check company, also commonly referred to as a special purpose acquisition company, or SPAC, formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, recapitalization, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses.

data.description:

  • INOVIO delivers a new nonsurgical treatment option with a broad indication for adults living with RRP, a rare and debilitating disease that often requires surgery
  • VOCERYQ™ is a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy that targets the root cause of RRP: HPV-6 and HPV-11
  • INOVIO expects to make VOCERYQ available to order and ship in approximately 60 days, with full commercial launch in the first quarter of 2027
  • VOCERYQ represents the first U.S. FDA approved DNA medicine, validating INOVIO's novel platform technology
  • INOVIO will host a conference call Monday, November 2, 2026 at 8:00 AM ET

PLYMOUTH MEETING, Pa., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- INOVIO (NASDAQ: INO), a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing DNA medicines to help treat and protect people from HPV-related diseases, cancer, and infectious diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval for VOCERYQ (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd), previously referred to as INO-3107, to reduce the frequency of surgery in adults with RRP. This indication is approved under the accelerated approval program based on demonstrated complete response defined as no requirement for surgical intervention in the 12 months after treatment in the efficacy population. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent on verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory study(ies). 

"With the approval of VOCERYQ, we believe our DNA medicine platform has the potential to transform the treatment paradigm for RRP by offering a patient-centric treatment option. VOCERYQ is designed to deliver what we understand matters most to patients, which is the reduction of the surgical burden caused by RRP," said Dr. Jacqueline Shea, INOVIO's President and Chief Executive Officer. "INOVIO is grateful to the patients, study investigators, and the RRP Foundation, who helped make this achievement possible, and also to the FDA, who recognized the significant unmet need in this patient community. We would like to thank our dedicated INOVIO team and their ongoing commitment to patients. We look forward to delivering VOCERYQ to the RRP community and believe it has the potential to become a new standard of care for this devastating disease."

The approval is supported by data from INOVIO's RRP-001 study which evaluated VOCERYQ in 32 adult patients with RRP who had two or more surgeries in the year prior to treatment. During the VOCERYQ dosing window, no additional papilloma surgical excisions were required in the protocol. Of the 32 patients, 26 patients required 3 or more surgeries for papilloma excision in the 12 months prior to treatment and were included in the efficacy evaluation (median number of surgical excisions in the 12 months prior to the first dose in the efficacy population was 4.5 (range: 3 to 8)). Seven out of the 26 patients (27% [95% CI: 12; 48%]) demonstrated a complete response, defined as requiring no surgical excision of papillomas, after 12 months of follow up, which is not expected as part of the natural history of the disease when untreated. The complete clinical data for VOCERYQ were published in Nature Communications and in The Laryngoscope, the leading journal for the specialists who treat RRP. 

"This new FDA-approved therapy brings us an important step closer to ensuring every RRP patient has access to a non-surgical treatment option that works for them. In reaching this milestone, we have shown that patient voices matter in the drug development process," said Kim McClellan, President of the RRP Foundation. "Patients have often had to endure repeated surgeries to control their RRP disease, but now thanks to the INOVIO team and the patients and investigators involved in the clinical development program for VOCERYQ, a new option is available that has the potential to further transform the treatment landscape for RRP patients. We look forward to continuing to work with clinicians, regulators and our partners in the healthcare industry to further improve the quality of life for those living with RRP."

Dr. Simon Best, Associate Professor of Otolaryngology at Johns Hopkins University and a lead investigator for INOVIO's RRP-001 study, said, "The approval of VOCERYQ is an important step in improving the quality of life for RRP patients as every surgery carries the risk of laryngeal injury. I believe it is in the best interest of RRP patients that the standard of care quickly transition away from surgical interventions to immunotherapy after RRP is diagnosed."

VOCERYQ was found to be well tolerated, with the most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) including injection site reactions, headache, fatigue, hypertension, nausea and dizziness. Most treatment-related adverse reactions were grade 1 and 2 and transient. There were no grade 4 or 5 common adverse events. All 32 patients completed the study. See additional Important Safety Information below.

To verify the clinical benefit of VOCERYQ, a confirmatory study is expected to be conducted. The FDA requires INOVIO to submit a draft protocol for the study by the end of 2026 with the expectation of aligning on a final protocol by mid-2027.

VOCERYQ was approved in combination with CELLECTRA® 5PSP, INOVIO's proprietary DNA medicine delivery device. INOVIO expects to make VOCERYQ available to order and ship in approximately 60 days and anticipates full field deployment during the first quarter of 2027. INOVIO has engaged Syneos Health to support the recruitment and deployment of our medical and commercial field teams.

Conference Call 
INOVIO will host a conference call on Monday, November 2 at 8:00 AM ET to provide additional details regarding the approval, including key aspects of the label and commercialization. You can watch the webcast at https://app.webinar.net/6LNlx7kxyqd. Event details can be found on INOVIO's website in the Events & Presentations section at https://ir.inovio.com/events-and-presentations/default.aspx.

North American Toll Free: 1-800-836-8184

About RRP 
RRP is a rare, debilitating disease caused primarily by HPV-6 and/or HPV-11. RRP is characterized by the development of small, wart-like growths, or papillomas, in the respiratory tract. While papillomas are generally benign, they can cause severe, life-threatening airway obstruction and respiratory complications. RRP can also significantly affect quality of life for patients by affecting the voice box, limiting the ability to speak effectively. Surgery to remove papillomas is the current standard of care for RRP; however, the papillomas often grow back. INOVIO's market research to date with patients and healthcare professionals indicates that a reduction of even one surgery matters, because every surgery poses a significant risk of causing permanent damage to the vocal cords and comes with potential costs to the patient, including adverse impacts to both quality of life and finances. Based on ongoing analysis of claims data, INOVIO believes there is a prevalent population of at least 25,000 patients with RRP in the United States, with additional patients diagnosed each year.

About VOCERYQ™
VOCERYQ™ is a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy designed to reduce the frequency of surgery for adults with RRP. VOCERYQ targets the root cause of RRP by generating an immune response using DNA plasmids that encode for HPV-6 and HPV-11 antigens. VOCERYQ is administered using the CELLECTRA® delivery device. Following a standard-of-care surgical debulking of visible papilloma prior to the initial administration of VOCERYQ, no additional surgical intervention is required as part of the 9-week dosing regimen. 

The FDA previously granted VOCERYQ both Orphan Drug and Breakthrough Therapy designations, and the European Commission granted INO-3107 Orphan Drug designation.

Learn more at www.voceryq.com.

INDICATION
VOCERYQ is indicated to reduce the frequency of surgical papilloma excisions in adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in the frequency of surgical papilloma excisions. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory study(ies).

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION 
Warnings & Precautions: Injection site reactions have occurred with VOCERYQ injection. Monitor patients for local site reactions for at least 30 minutes after treatment and manage accordingly.

Electroporation Related Adverse Reactions: Procedure-related effects including muscle contractions, transient bleeding, and vasovagal reactions may occur. Avoid use in patients with ipsilateral ICDs/pacemakers, metal implants or skin abnormalities at treatment site.

Adverse Reactions: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) are injection site reactions, headache, fatigue, hypertension, nausea and dizziness.

Please go to www.voceryq.com for full Prescribing Information, including Patient Information. 

About INOVIO's DNA Medicines Platform
INOVIO's DNA medicines platform has two innovative components: precisely designed DNA plasmids, delivered by INOVIO's proprietary medical device, CELLECTRA. INOVIO uses proprietary technology to design its DNA plasmids, which are small circular DNA molecules that enable the body's cells to produce specific proteins to target and fight disease. INOVIO's proprietary CELLECTRA delivery devices are designed to optimally deliver its DNA medicines to the body's cells without requiring chemical adjuvants or lipid nanoparticles and without the risk of the anti-vector response historically seen with viral vector platforms.

About INOVIO
INOVIO is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing innovative DNA medicines to help treat and protect people from HPV-related diseases, cancer, and infectious diseases. INOVIO's technology optimizes the design and delivery of DNA medicines that enable the body to manufacture its own disease-fighting tools.
